mainTopic: The drinking of the סוטה: what the repeated 'he shall make her drink' teaches, the order of the drinking and the מנחה, and when she may refuse
overview: A ברייתא asks why the תורה keeps repeating 'he shall make her drink' about the סוטה. רבי עקיבא learns that once the מגילה is erased into the water, she is made to drink even if she refuses. רבי שמעון learns from 'and afterward' that three things must come first: the קומץ is offered, the מגילה is fully erased, and she accepts the שבועה. The גמרא explains each condition. רב אשי says the erasing must be so complete that no mark of the ink still shows, and the condition about the שבועה is explained as worded loosely, since the מגילה is not even written before the שבועה. Next the גמרא shows how the רבנן and רבי שמעון each read the three פסוקים about drinking: the רבנן say she drinks before the מנחה, and רבי שמעון says the מנחה comes first. Finally the גמרא asks whether רבי עקיבא really holds she is forced to drink. It concludes that a calm refusal counts as an admission, so she never drinks. A refusal out of fear lets her back out only until the קומץ is offered, and after that she is made to drink.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Once the scroll is erased, she is made to drink
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the פסוק says 'he shall make her drink' twice. רבי עקיבא learns from the extra mention that once the מגילה has been erased, the סוטה is made to drink even against her will.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Why does the פסוק say 'And he shall make her drink'? It was already said earlier, 'And he shall make her drink.' It teaches that if the מגילה was already erased and then she says 'I will not drink,' they force her and make her drink against her will. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא points out that the same words appear twice in the סוטה section. רבי עקיבא explains that the extra words teach that she is forced to drink once the scroll has been erased.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not waste words, so the second 'he shall make her drink' must add something new. רבי עקיבא says the addition is a law about forcing: after the holy name has been erased into the water, she cannot back out. The extra words show that the drinking will happen no matter what.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? It is used when a phrase seems extra.
The scroll was erased. The written curses, which include God's name, are dissolved into the water.
They force her. This is a strong word for making her do it.
Against her will.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Why does the verse say 'And he shall make her drink'?
But it was already said, 'And he shall make her drink'!
To teach that if the scroll was erased
and she says 'I will not drink'

phrases.aramaic: מְעַרְעֲרִין אוֹתָהּ וּמַשְׁקִין אוֹתָהּ בְּעַל כׇּרְחָהּ,
phrases.english: they force her and make her drink against her will,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא with רבי עקיבא's reading of the repeated phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the מגילה is erased, the סוטה is made to drink even against her will (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: רבי שמעון: Three things must happen before she drinks
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads the words 'and afterward he shall make her drink' differently. They mean she drinks only after everything mentioned earlier is done, so three things hold up the drinking: the קומץ, the erased מגילה, and accepting the שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Why does the פסוק say 'and afterward he shall make her drink'? It already said 'And he shall make her drink.' It means after all the actions mentioned above. This teaches that three things hold her back from drinking: until the קומץ is offered, until the מגילה is erased, and until she accepts the שבועה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives his own explanation of the repeated words. He says the word 'afterward' sets the order: she drinks only after all the earlier steps are finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learned a rule about forcing her. רבי שמעון focuses on the word 'afterward' and learns a rule about order. Three things are required first, and if any one is missing, she may not drink yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And afterward he shall make her drink. This comes in the פסוק right after the burning of the קומץ.
It tells us. The פסוק is teaching this.
Hold back or prevent. These are things that must be done first.
The handful taken from the מנחה and burned on the מזבח.
The oath the כהן gives the סוטה, which she accepts by saying 'אמן'.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the three conditions that the גמרא explains one at a time in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״וְאַחַר יַשְׁקֶה״ מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר?
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Why does the verse say 'and afterward he shall make her drink'?
But it was already said, 'And he shall make her drink'!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, לְאַחַר כׇּל מַעֲשִׂים כּוּלָּן הָאֲמוּרִין לְמַעְלָה.
phrases.english: Rather, it means after all the actions mentioned above.
It teaches that three things hold her back from drinking:
until the handful has been offered,
and until the scroll has been erased,
and until she has accepted the oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״וְאַחַר יַשְׁקֶה״ מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same repeated phrase that רבי עקיבא explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה does not drink until the קומץ is offered, the מגילה is erased, and she accepts the שבועה (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: The first condition fits רבי שמעון's view on the order of the service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first condition, that the קומץ must be offered first. This matches רבי שמעון's known opinion that her מנחה is offered before she drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Until the קומץ is offered': רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, since he said that the כהן offers her מנחה and only afterward makes her drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes through רבי שמעון's three conditions one at a time. The first one fits with something רבי שמעון already said about the order of the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was an earlier disagreement about which comes first, the drinking or the מנחה. רבי שמעון holds that the מנחה comes first, so it makes sense that, for him, the קומץ holds up the drinking. No new difficulty comes up here; this condition is consistent with his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning. He is consistent with what he said elsewhere.
Offers a קרבן on the מזבח.
Her מנחה, the flour offering brought for the סוטה.

phrases.english: 'Until the handful has been offered.'
Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, as he said:

phrases.aramaic: מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַשְׁקָהּ.
phrases.english: He offers her meal-offering and afterward makes her drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרַב הַקּוֹמֶץ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of רבי שמעון's three conditions from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קומץ condition matches רבי שמעון's view that the מנחה is offered before the drinking.

steps.title: Why say the scroll must be erased? That seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the second condition. If the מגילה was not erased into the water, what would she even be drinking? The condition seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Until the מגילה is erased': But otherwise, what would he give her to drink?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second condition and challenges it. It seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'bitter water' gets its power from the erased writing. Without the erasing there is nothing to drink but plain water, so of course she cannot drink before it is erased. The question is why רבי שמעון needed to list this at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But otherwise, what? This introduces a challenge showing that the alternative makes no sense.
He gives her to drink.

phrases.english: 'Until the scroll has been erased.'
But otherwise, what would he give her to drink?
phrases.notes: Without the erased writing in it, the water is just ordinary water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first condition to the second and questions why it is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second condition in רבי שמעון's list: 'until the מגילה is erased.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without erasing, there is no special water to drink, so the condition seems pointless to state.

steps.title: רב אשי: The ink is gone but its mark still shows
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the condition is needed when the writing was erased but a visible mark of it is still left on the parchment. She may not drink until the מגילה is fully erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It was needed only for a case where the mark of the writing can still be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by pointing to a case where the condition really adds something. Even when most of the ink is in the water, she waits until no mark is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the only options were 'erased' or 'not erased at all.' רב אשי points to a middle case: the ink was washed off but a faint mark still shows. רבי שמעון's condition teaches that this partial erasing is not enough, and the erasing must be complete before she drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for a particular case. This introduces the case the law is really talking about.
Its mark or impression, the trace of the ink left on the parchment.
Noticeable or visible.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the סוטה drinks only after three things: the קומץ is offered, the מגילה is completely erased (with not even a visible mark left), and she accepts the שבועה. According to רבי עקיבא, once the מגילה is erased, she is made to drink even if she refuses.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the writing was never erased. The ink is in the water, but a visible trace on the parchment is enough to hold up the drinking.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It was needed only
for where its mark can still be seen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לֹא נִצְרְכָה לְשֶׁרִישּׁוּמוֹ נִיכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 by narrowing the condition to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing to a specific case (לא נצרכה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that once the ink is in the water she may drink, even if a faint mark remains on the parchment.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may not drink until the מגילה is completely erased, with no visible mark left.

steps.title: Is the scroll written before she accepts the oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's third condition, because it seems to allow writing the מגילה before the שבועה, against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Until she accepts the oath.' This suggests that only the drinking waits for the oath, but the scroll may already be written. But רבא said that a סוטה scroll written before she accepted the oath is worth nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the third condition, 'she does not drink until she accepts the שבועה,' and finds a problem with how it is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the drinking waits for the שבועה, then the writing of the מגילה could come earlier. But רבא rules that a מגילה written before the שבועה is invalid. So the condition seems to say something that cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: drinking
writing
but didn't (he) say? Opens a challenge from another teaching
he did nothing at all, the act does not count

phrases.english: Until she accepts the oath upon herself.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting רבי שמעון's third condition from step 2.

phrases.english: It is only drinking that she does not drink (before the oath),
but writing, they do write (the scroll) for her?
But didn't רבא say:
A סוטה scroll that he wrote
before she accepted the oath upon herself —
he has done nothing at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining conditions one and two, the גמרא now examines the third condition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי שמעון's third condition, that the drinking waits for the שבועה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording suggests the מגילה may already be written before the שבועה, but רבא says such a מגילה is invalid.

steps.title: The phrase was said along with the others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the third condition was simply listed together with the others and should not be read too closely.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was cited for no special reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the third condition was just said alongside the first two, without meaning anything extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In truth the מגילה is not even written before the שבועה, so we should not infer that writing may come first. The wording 'she does not drink' was used only to match the other conditions.

keyTerms.meaning: he cited it for no special reason, just to fit with the others

phrases.english: He cited it for no reason.
phrases.notes: It was only listed to go along with the other two conditions, so don't learn anything from its wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing the inference: the wording was not chosen carefully enough to learn from.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the wording teaches that the מגילה may be written before the שבועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording teaches nothing extra; the מגילה is written only after the שבועה, as רבא says.
steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבי שמעון's conditions are now explained: the קומץ comes first, the מגילה must be fully erased, and the שבועה comes before everything, even the writing.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן and רבי שמעון really disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, setting up an explanation of the source behind the argument between the רבנן and רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say she drinks first and then the מנחה is offered, while רבי שמעון says the מנחה comes first. The גמרא wants to know which פסוקים each side is reading, and how.

keyTerms.meaning: about what do they disagree? Asks for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" are the רבנן and רבי שמעון, who argue about whether the drinking or the מנחה comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי שמעון's conditions to asking about the source of the whole argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוקים are behind the argument, and how each side reads them.

steps.title: Three verses say 'he shall make her drink'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the תורה says 'he shall make her drink' three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three verses are written: the first 'and he shall make her drink,' then 'and afterward he shall make her drink,' and the last 'and he shall make her drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by listing the three פסוקים. This sets up how each side will use them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are three mentions, each side must give a reason for every one. The argument comes down to which פסוק teaches the main order and what the other two teach.

keyTerms.meaning: verses
the first
the last

phrases.english: Three verses are written:
The first, "And he shall make her drink,"
"And afterward he shall make her drink,"
and the last, "And he shall make her drink."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about how to use the three mentions of 'he shall make her drink'.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the three verses
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the first פסוק for the order (drink, then מנחה), the second for a still-visible mark, and the third for forcing her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: the first 'and he shall make her drink' teaches the law itself, that he makes her drink and afterward offers her מנחה. 'And afterward he shall make her drink' is needed for when the mark of the writing is still visible. The last 'and he shall make her drink' teaches that if the scroll was erased and she says 'I will not drink,' she is forced to drink against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each of the three פסוקים teaches according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the first פסוק comes before the מנחה is mentioned, the רבנן learn that drinking comes first. The words 'and afterward' then teach that she drinks only after the writing is fully gone. The last mention teaches forced drinking once the מגילה is erased.

keyTerms.meaning: for its own plain meaning, to teach the main law
he needs it (to teach something else)
its mark is visible
they force her (to drink)
against her will

phrases.english: The רבנן hold:
The first "And he shall make her drink" is for itself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמַּשְׁקֶה וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ.
phrases.english: that he makes her drink and afterward offers her meal-offering.
"And afterward he shall make her drink" —
he needs it for when its mark is still visible.
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי's case from step 5: the writing is erased but a mark is still left, so she may not drink yet.

phrases.english: The last "And he shall make her drink" —
that if the scroll was erased
and she says, "I will not drink,"
they force her
and he makes her drink against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the three פסוקים listed in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן: first פסוק = drink before the מנחה; second = not while the mark is visible; third = forced drinking after erasing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן she drinks first and then her מנחה is offered.

steps.title: How רבי שמעון reads the three verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses the second פסוק for the order (מנחה, then drink), the first to teach that the reverse order still works after the fact, and the third for forcing her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds: 'And afterward he shall make her drink' teaches the law itself, that he offers her מנחה and afterward makes her drink. The first 'and he shall make her drink' teaches that if he made her drink and afterward offered her מנחה, it is valid. The last 'and he shall make her drink' teaches that if the scroll was erased and she said 'I will not drink,' they force her and make her drink against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי שמעון's reading of the same three פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and afterward' come right after the מנחה in the תורה, so רבי שמעון learns that the מנחה comes first. The first פסוק, which mentions drinking earlier, teaches that if they did it in the other order, the מנחה still counts. Both sides agree on what the last פסוק teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: holds, is of the opinion
her meal-offering
valid

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree there are three mentions and that the last one teaches forced drinking. They argue only about which פסוק sets the order: the רבנן say drink first, רבי שמעון says מנחה first (but the other order still counts after the fact).
steps.confusionAlert: Earlier (step 5) רב אשי used the 'mark still visible' rule for רבי שמעון, but here רבי שמעון uses 'and afterward' for the order. For him, the 'visible mark' rule comes from his reading in step 2: drink only after everything is fully done.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון holds:
"And afterward he shall make her drink" is for itself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמַּקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַשְׁקָהּ.
phrases.english: that he offers her meal-offering and afterward makes her drink.
The first "And he shall make her drink" —
that if he made her drink and afterward
offered her meal-offering, it is valid.
The last "And he shall make her drink" —
that if the scroll was erased
and she said, "I will not drink,"
they force her
and they make her drink against her will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the argument, matching the רבנן's reading in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי שמעון: second פסוק = מנחה before drinking; first = the reverse order is valid after the fact; third = forced drinking after erasing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון the מנחה is offered first and then she drinks, but if done in reverse the מנחה is still valid.

steps.title: The רבנן's reply: a verse does not open with an after-the-fact rule
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי שמעון's use of the first פסוק as a בדיעבד rule, because the תורה does not begin with what is only valid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: a פסוק does not open with a rule that only works after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן do not accept רבי שמעון's reading of the first 'he shall make her drink'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said the first mention teaches that drinking before the מנחה still works בדיעבד. The רבנן answer that the תורה would not start the topic with a backup rule. So the first mention must be describing the proper order: drink first, then the מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: after the fact; it still counts once done, even if it was not the proper way
opened, began
the פסוק, the verse

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: drink first, then the מנחה, since the first mention is the main order. רבי שמעון: the מנחה comes first, and drinking first still works בדיעבד.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
The verse does not open with an after-the-fact rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reason for rejecting רבי שמעון's reading in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first mention of drinking cannot be a בדיעבד rule, because a פסוק does not open with one.

steps.title: Does רבי עקיבא really hold she is forced to drink?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי עקיבא holds she is forced to drink, using a ברייתא where he says there is no point in forcing her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי עקיבא really hold that she is made to drink against her will? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says they put an iron hook in her mouth. If the scroll was already erased and she says 'I won't drink', they force her mouth open and make her drink. רבי עקיבא said: The whole point is only to test her. Her refusal already shows the answer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the teaching that she is forced to drink. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא seems to say she is never forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says that once the scroll is erased into the water, she is forced to drink even with an iron hook. רבי עקיבא answers that the water is only meant to test her. If she refuses, that refusal acts like an admission of guilt, so there is nothing left to test and no reason to force her.

keyTerms.meaning: against her will, by force
an iron hook, used to hold the mouth open
the scroll was erased, meaning the written פרשה was dissolved into the water
they force her mouth open
she already stands tested; her guilt is already clear

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying she is innocent. He means the opposite: her refusal shows guilt, so the test is no longer needed.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Akiva hold
that they make her drink against her will?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
An iron hook
is placed into her mouth,
so that if the scroll was erased
and she said, "I will not drink,"
they force her mouth open
and make her drink against her will.
Rabbi Akiva said:
Do we need anything other than to test her?
But she already stands tested!
phrases.notes: By refusing to drink, she is basically admitting guilt, so there is nothing left to check.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַשְׁקִין אוֹתָהּ בְּעַל כׇּרְחָהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening ברייתא (step 1), where רבי עקיבא taught that she is forced to drink. It checks that teaching against רבי עקיבא's own words in another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the סוטה is forced to drink, as held by רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא רבי עקיבא says forcing makes no sense, because her refusal already proves her guilt.

steps.title: Answer: she can back out only before the handful is offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רבי עקיבא as talking about before the קומץ is offered. After that point she cannot back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: before the קומץ is offered, she can back out. Once the קומץ is offered, she cannot back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רבי עקיבא's words to an earlier stage of the process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's 'no need to force her' applies only before the קומץ from her מנחה is offered. After the קומץ is offered, she is forced to drink. So רבי עקיבא can still hold that she is forced, but only at the later stage.

was offered
to back out, to take back her agreement

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13 by limiting when רבי עקיבא's statement applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a statement to a specific stage (אוקימתא by timing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא holds she is never forced to drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before the קומץ she may back out. After the קומץ she is forced to drink.

steps.title: But the same reasoning should apply after the handful too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if her refusal proves guilt, it should prove guilt after the קומץ as well, so why can't she back out then?
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your own reasoning, this itself is a problem: once the קומץ is offered she can't back out? Her refusal still shows the answer!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, using רבי עקיבא's own reason against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reason was that refusing acts like an admission of guilt. That reason does not depend on timing. So the challenge asks why her refusal after the קומץ should not also count as an admission, which would mean there is no need to force her then either.

keyTerms.meaning: and by your own reasoning
this itself should be a problem for you

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,
this itself should be difficult for you:
once the handful has been offered,
she cannot back out?
But she already stands tested!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 14 using רבי עקיבא's reasoning from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that after the קומץ she cannot back out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Refusal counts as an admission at any stage, so forcing her should never be needed, even after the קומץ.

steps.title: It depends on whether she refuses out of fear or with a clear mind
steps.stepSummary: Refusing out of fear is not an admission, so she is forced to drink. Refusing calmly is an admission, so she is not forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's not a problem. One case is where she backs out because she is shaking with fear. The other case is where she backs out while healthy and calm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by splitting it into two kinds of refusal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she backs out because she is trembling with fear, that does not show guilt, since even an innocent woman may be scared. In that case she is forced to drink. If she backs out calmly and clearly, her refusal counts as an admission, and that is when רבי עקיבא says she 'already stands tested'.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; both statements can be true
trembling, fear
good health; a calm, steady state

steps.whatToRemember: A סוטה who backs out after the קומץ out of fear is forced to drink. One who backs out calmly is treated as having admitted guilt and is not forced.
steps.confusionAlert: Which 'this' is which: backing out from fear is the case where she is forced. Backing out while calm is the case where she is 'already tested'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This lets רבי עקיבא hold both that she can be forced to drink and that refusal can count as an admission. Each rule fits a different situation.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

because of trembling fear,
phrases.notes: This is the case where, once the קומץ is offered, she is forced to drink, since fear alone doesn't show she is guilty.

phrases.english: and that case is where she backs out
while in a healthy, calm state.
phrases.notes: Backing out calmly looks like an admission, so this is when she 'already stands tested'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — דְּקָהָדְרָא בַּהּ מֵחֲמַת רְתִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15 by telling apart two kinds of refusal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any refusal counts as an admission, so she should never be forced.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a calm refusal counts as an admission. A refusal from fear does not, so then she is forced to drink.

steps.title: Rereading רבי עקיבא: calm refusal versus fearful refusal, before and after the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the full, corrected reading of רבי עקיבא's ברייתא. A calm refusal means she never drinks. A fearful refusal lets her back out only until the קומץ is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי עקיבא means. Whenever she refuses while calm and healthy, she does not drink at all. If she refuses out of fear, and the קומץ has not yet been offered, she can back out. That holds when the מגילה has not been erased yet. It also holds if the מגילה was already erased, because the כהנים erased it too early. Once the קומץ has been offered, the כהנים erased the מגילה at the proper time, so she can no longer back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the last few steps by explaining exactly what רבי עקיבא's ברייתא is saying. It brings together the timing answer from step 14 and the fear-versus-calm answer from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calm refusal is treated as an admission of guilt, so at any stage she simply does not drink. A refusal out of fear is not an admission, so the only question is timing. Until the קומץ is offered, any erasing of the מגילה was done out of order, so it does not lock her in. After the קומץ, the erasing was done properly, and she must drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Good health; here, refusing while calm and steady, not out of panic
Trembling or fear
The handful of her מנחה offering that the כהן burns on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Calm refusal means she never drinks, because it is an admission. Fearful refusal lets her back out before the קומץ, even after the מגילה was erased. After the קומץ, she is forced to drink.
steps.confusionAlert: Erasing the מגילה is not the point of no return. The offering of the קומץ is. If the מגילה was erased before the קומץ, that was done out of order, so she can still back out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the challenge from step 13. רבי עקיבא's 'no point in forcing her' refers to a calm refusal, or to a fearful refusal before the קומץ. So he can still hold that after the קומץ she is forced to drink.

phrases.english: And this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא. The גמרא is now explaining his ברייתא from step 13.

phrases.english: In any case where she refuses while calm and healthy,
she does not drink at all.
If she refuses out of fear,
before the handful has been offered,
when the scroll has not yet been erased,
or even if the scroll was already erased,
since the priests acted improperly in erasing it,
she can back out.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Once the handful has been offered,
in which case the priests acted properly in erasing it,
she cannot back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the fear-versus-calm distinction from step 16 and the before-and-after-the-קומץ distinction from step 14. It fits both into one complete reading of רבי עקיבא's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the ברייתא that combines two distinctions: calm versus fear, and before versus after the קומץ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's statement that there is no point in forcing her seemed to say she is never forced to drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is never forced if she refuses calmly. If she refuses out of fear, she is forced only after the קומץ is offered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A calm refusal is an admission, so she does not drink at any stage. A fearful refusal allows her to back out until the קומץ is offered, even if the מגילה was already erased too early. After the קומץ is offered she cannot back out and is made to drink.
